title: The Cover-up
subtitle: Test your understanding of The Cover-up — the hand-off from a garden find to the Smithsonian, the NDA, and the hoax label.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.body: A skull under a vegetable patch is enough to start a chain the finder thinks is ordinary help. By the time the suits leave, the photographs are gone, the speech is signed away, and the bones are in a vault the public does not enter.

questions.question: What event activates the cover-up operational protocol?

options.label: A
options.text: Civilian or domestic excavation projects unearthing physical artifacts or anomalous skeletal remains.
options.rationale: The protocol activates when private excavations, domestic groundwork, or civilian projects breach the soil and uncover anomalous skeletal remains.

options.label: B
options.text: An official directive from international judicial bodies to audit private land ownership across several counties.
options.rationale: The protocol starts at a soil breach, not at a judicial audit of land titles.

options.label: C
options.text: Public broadcasts of unverified civilian sightings that have already left the site.
options.rationale: The apparatus intercepts physical evidence at the point of contact, before a public broadcast.

options.label: D
options.text: The publication of unauthorized research papers by independent historians.
options.rationale: Papers are later talk, while the trigger is an undeniable physical find in the ground.

questions.hint: Look at the groundwork that uncovers material the public narrative cannot hold.

questions.question: How is the Smithsonian Institution characterized in this account?

options.label: A
options.text: The archaeological vault
options.rationale: The vault is where remains are kept, not the name given to the institution itself.

options.label: B
options.text: A regional museum department
options.rationale: A regional museum is an earlier hand-off, not the name used for the Smithsonian.

options.label: C
options.text: The municipal police station
options.rationale: The police station escalates the call, and it is not the characterization of the Smithsonian.

options.label: D
options.text: The Vatican of Archaeology
options.rationale: The Smithsonian is the centralized institutional authority operating as the Vatican of Archaeology, responsible for initiating formal recovery operations and locking anomalous skeletal remains away.

questions.hint: Check the Key Terminology name used for that centralized authority.

questions.question: What is the primary operational role of the Official Suits at an excavation site?

options.label: A
options.text: Filing zoning violations so the city can take the parcel through an ordinary land case and then reopen the garden for a public viewing.
options.rationale: The on-site work is the NDA, the photographs, and the threats, not a zoning filing.

options.label: B
options.text: Paying the finder a fee in exchange for a voluntary gift of the specimen.
options.rationale: Compliance is forced under duress, not bought as a voluntary donation.

options.label: C
options.text: Seizing private documentation, enforcing non-disclosure agreements, and delivering personal threats.
options.rationale: Official Suits arrive to execute non-disclosure agreements, seize private documentation, and deliver personal threats.

options.label: D
options.text: Running open radiocarbon dating and a public peer review of the remains on the lawn.
options.rationale: The protocol skips open scientific review and moves straight to seizure and silence.

questions.hint: Read the Key Terminology line for the people who arrive in official vehicles.

questions.question: Why do frontline police officers escalate a discovery to their station superiors?

options.label: A
options.text: They must hand every forensic scene to a state coroner before anyone else.
options.rationale: The station hands the notice to a university or museum, not to a coroner.

options.label: B
options.text: They already know the bones belong in a restricted federal collection.
options.rationale: The officers are unsure how to proceed, and they do not arrive knowing an institutional owner.

options.label: C
options.text: They suspect the dig breaks local environmental protection rules.
options.rationale: The escalation is about the scale of the anatomical find, not an environmental charge.

options.label: D
options.text: They lack both the protocol and the authority to interpret an anatomical anomaly of this scale.
options.rationale: Responding officers possess neither the protocol nor the authority to interpret a discovery of such immense physical scale.

questions.hint: See what those officers lack when the find is on this scale.

questions.question: In the escalation pipeline, who receives the notice directly after police station personnel?

options.label: A
options.text: Historians and mainstream media assigned to brand the find
options.rationale: The hoax work comes after custody, not as the step right after the station.

options.label: B
options.text: A local university or regional museum department
options.rationale: Senior personnel hand off the notification to a local university or regional museum department.

options.label: C
options.text: Men in official suits already waiting at the garden gate
options.rationale: The suits arrive once recovery is underway, after the academic hand-off.

options.label: D
options.text: The Smithsonian Institution
options.rationale: The university or museum contacts the Smithsonian, so the station does not call it first.

questions.hint: Name the academic step between the station and the apex institution.

questions.question: What role does the Hoax Narrative play in the containment strategy?

options.label: A
options.text: It teaches the public how to tell a real fossil from a cast.
options.rationale: The label is used to invalidate documented finds, not to train the public in fossil identification.

options.label: B
options.text: It supplies a standardized debunking story that publicly invalidates documented discoveries.
options.rationale: The Hoax Narrative is the standardized cover story used to publicly invalidate documented anomalous discoveries as fables, myths, or fraudulent claims.

options.label: C
options.text: It gives discoverers a defense against an NDA penalty.
options.rationale: The hoax label is aimed at the public record, not offered to the finder as a defense.

options.label: D
options.text: It warns researchers about fraud inside ordinary field work and tells a regional museum department which specimens to turn away at the door.
options.rationale: The label discredits genuine physical evidence, rather than policing ordinary research fraud.

questions.hint: Look at how surviving public reports are treated.

questions.question: What dimensions are given for the giant human skull in the garden example?

options.label: A
options.text: Two meters in height and 1.5 meters in width
options.rationale: The example is a massive human skull measuring two meters in height and 1.5 meters in width beneath a domestic garden vegetable patch.

options.label: B
options.text: One meter in height and one meter in width
options.rationale: One meter by one meter is smaller than the skull described in that garden example.

options.label: C
options.text: Five meters in height and three meters in width
options.rationale: Those figures are larger than the garden skull, which is two meters by 1.5 meters.

options.label: D
options.text: Three meters in height and two meters in width
options.rationale: The garden example is two meters in height and 1.5 meters in width, not three by two.

questions.hint: Check the skull named under the domestic vegetable patch.

questions.question: What leverage is used to enforce compliance with the Non-Disclosure Agreement?

options.label: A
options.text: Prolonged imprisonment, complete forfeiture of home and vehicle, and destruction of family security.
options.rationale: The leverage includes prolonged imprisonment, the complete forfeiture of home and vehicle, and the destruction of family security, with institutional eyes and ears continuously watching and listening.

options.label: B
options.text: Compulsory relocation to an isolated administrative territory.
options.rationale: Relocation is not among the penalties named for the signer.

options.label: C
options.text: A civil fine paid to the local police department.
options.rationale: The pressure described is personal ruin, not a routine fine.

options.label: D
options.text: Loss of an academic license, a lasting ban on public employment, and removal from the regional museum department that first received the notice.
options.rationale: The finders are ordinary civilians, and the threats named are imprisonment, the home, and the family.

questions.hint: Read the coercion line about home, vehicle, and family security.

questions.question: Where are the anomalous skeletal remains kept after they leave the civilian site?

options.label: A
options.text: In an off-site university laboratory archive.
options.rationale: The university is an intermediary, while lasting custody is the institutional vault.

options.label: B
options.text: In sealed subterranean vaults, away from civilian observation.
options.rationale: The Smithsonian locks anomalous skeletal remains away in sealed subterranean vaults, sealed away from civilian observation.

options.label: C
options.text: In a high-security police evidence locker.
options.rationale: Police hand the matter on, and they do not keep the bones.

options.label: D
options.text: In a restricted display wing of a national museum, set beside ordinary human exhibits that stay open to civilian visitors.
options.rationale: The protocol keeps this evidence off public museum floors.

questions.hint: See where the Smithsonian locks the remains.

questions.question: Which historical projects are named as unearthing thousands of giant skeletal remains?

options.label: A
options.text: Historical railway expansions cutting through ancient burial mounds.
options.rationale: Historical railway expansions through burial mounds unearthed thousands of giant skeletal remains.

options.label: B
options.text: Routine municipal road repairs beside police stations.
options.rationale: Road repairs beside a station are not the projects named for those thousands of remains.

options.label: C
options.text: Vegetable-patch digging under domestic houses.
options.rationale: The garden patch is the single-skull example, not the mass railway finds.

options.label: D
options.text: Home extensions, conservatories, and ordinary garden plots.
options.rationale: Those domestic digs start single finds, while the thousands are tied to railway work through burial mounds.

questions.hint: Look at the infrastructure named together with burial mounds.

questions.question: What size range is given for the giant skeletal remains from those railway expansions?

options.label: A
options.text: Eight feet to fifteen feet tall
options.rationale: That band misses the upper figure of over thirty-five meters.

options.label: B
options.text: Fifty meters to one hundred meters tall
options.rationale: The upper figure given is over thirty-five meters, not one hundred.

options.label: C
options.text: Twelve feet to over thirty-five meters tall
options.rationale: The remains are giant skeletal remains ranging from twelve feet to over thirty-five meters tall.

options.label: D
options.text: Six feet to eight feet tall
options.rationale: That range is ordinary human height, not the giant scale named here.

questions.hint: Check the lower and upper heights named with the burial-mound finds.

questions.question: Why do civilian discoverers inadvertently start their own silencing?

options.label: A
options.text: They instinctively trust and contact local municipal services after the find.
options.rationale: Everyday discoverers instinctively trust and contact local municipal services, and that call starts the chain that silences them.

options.label: B
options.text: They wait so long that agents can call the site abandoned.
options.rationale: The chain starts when they notify the police, not when they delay.

options.label: C
options.text: They try to sell the specimen on an open market.
options.rationale: The account describes a good-faith municipal report, not a sale.

options.label: D
options.text: They post unverified photographs to a public board and draw ridicule before any regional museum department can look at the bones.
options.rationale: Photographs are taken, then seized, and the silencing starts with the municipal call.

questions.hint: See whom everyday finders trust enough to call.

questions.question: What happens to visual evidence when the operatives arrive?

options.label: A
options.text: Selected images are released to media outlets under an institutional mark so readers can set them beside historic newspaper accounts.
options.rationale: The point of the seizure is to stop visual proof from leaving the site.

options.label: B
options.text: Recordings are scrambled and then handed back to the finder.
options.rationale: The finder must surrender the captures, not receive a scrambled copy.

options.label: C
options.text: Photographs are filed in a municipal database for a later review.
options.rationale: The images are surrendered so they cannot circulate, not parked for a public review.

options.label: D
options.text: Discoverers must surrender all photographic records, digital captures, and physical recordings.
options.rationale: The discoverer is compelled to surrender all photographic evidence, digital captures, and physical recordings of the site.

questions.hint: Read the line about photographic records at the site.

questions.question: What keeps institutional control over human history in place?

options.label: A
options.text: Open agreement among researchers on a single evolutionary timeline, settled after the remains pass an open scientific review.
options.rationale: The insulation comes from containment and the hoax label, not from open agreement.

options.label: B
options.text: The total absence of any old newspaper account of anomalous finds.
options.rationale: Historic newspaper accounts exist and are aggressively debunked, rather than being absent.

options.label: C
options.text: Successful use of the hoax label, together with total containment, until systemic disclosure.
options.rationale: So long as institutions deploy the hoax label, consensus reality remains completely insulated from physical truth until systemic disclosure dismantles the apparatus.

options.label: D
options.text: A lack of public interest in older artifacts.
options.rationale: Interest is managed by discrediting finds, not by an absence of curiosity.

questions.hint: Read the closing line about the hoax label and physical truth.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the cover-up apparatus?

options.label: A
options.text: To take mineral and oil deposits under private land.
options.rationale: The targets are anomalous artifacts and skeletal remains, not mineral rights.

options.label: B
options.text: To neutralize direct empirical discoveries at the point of contact and keep the public from paradigm-breaking realities.
options.rationale: Its primary purpose is to neutralize direct empirical discoveries at the point of contact so the public stays insulated from paradigm-breaking realities.

options.label: C
options.text: To protect fragile ancient burial mounds from untrained civilian digging during historical railway expansions and later domestic garden work.
options.rationale: The stated purpose is containment of contradictory evidence, not site conservation.

options.label: D
options.text: To sell rare artifacts through private institutional auctions.
options.rationale: The finds are locked away, not sold.

questions.hint: Look at what the protocol does at the moment of a find.

questions.question: How does the apparatus handle direct witness testimony?

options.label: A
options.text: Witnesses are brought onto official research teams so their activity can be watched from inside.
options.rationale: Discoverers are isolated and silenced, not hired onto a research team.

options.label: B
options.text: Testimony is rewritten and issued under an academic pseudonym.
options.rationale: The testimony is eradicated, not republished under another name.

options.label: C
options.text: Witnesses are undone through a public character campaign.
options.rationale: The silence is secured by the NDA and the threats before a public campaign is required.

options.label: D
options.text: Primary witness testimony is eradicated through legal gagging, surveillance threats, and forced compliance.
options.rationale: The central truth is the absolute eradication of primary witness testimony, with discoverers completely separated from their physical evidence and stripped of speech.

questions.hint: See what happens to the finder speech and the proof together.

questions.question: Which international counterpart to the Smithsonian is named?

options.label: A
options.text: Authorities at a regional museum
options.rationale: The regional museum is the academic intermediary, not the named counterpart.

options.label: B
options.text: Authorities in London
options.rationale: The university or museum immediately contacts the Smithsonian or its international counterpart, such as authorities in London.

options.label: C
options.text: Authorities at a neighborhood university
options.rationale: The local university makes the call, and London is the counterpart named on the far side of it.

options.label: D
options.text: Authorities at the local police station
options.rationale: The station is the municipal step, not the international counterpart.

questions.hint: See which city is named beside the Smithsonian in the recovery step.

questions.question: What phase follows the academic intermediary notification?

options.label: A
options.text: Local disorientation and station escalation
options.rationale: That station step comes before the university is involved.

options.label: B
options.text: A municipal court hearing to impose the NDA
options.rationale: The NDA is signed on site with the suits, not issued first by a municipal court.

options.label: C
options.text: Apex Institutional Notification and Recovery
options.rationale: After the academic hand-off comes Apex Institutional Notification and Recovery, when the Smithsonian initiates the recovery protocol.

options.label: D
options.text: Public hoax deployment and media debunking
options.rationale: Debunking follows once the remains are already in custody.

questions.hint: Name the step in which specialized personnel come for the bones.

questions.question: What legal instrument is forced on civilian discoverers?

options.label: A
options.text: A land condemnation order
options.rationale: The home can be threatened, but the document they must sign is the non-disclosure agreement.

options.label: B
options.text: An archaeological salvage license
options.rationale: A salvage license would authorize digging, while this document bars speech.

options.label: C
options.text: A Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)
options.rationale: The NDA is a compulsory legal instrument that binds discoverers to absolute silence under penalty of catastrophic personal ruin.

options.label: D
options.text: A municipal indemnity waiver
options.rationale: The instrument binds the finder to silence, rather than waiving a financial claim.

questions.hint: Check the Key Terminology name for the compulsory silence document.

questions.question: How do historians and academic gatekeepers treat old public records of anomalies?

options.label: A
options.text: They aggressively debunk the records as hoaxes, fables, or fraudulent claims.
options.rationale: Historic newspaper accounts and civic records are aggressively debunked, and discoveries are officially branded as hoaxes.

options.label: B
options.text: They open new digs to test the old reports.
options.rationale: A new dig would risk more physical proof, which the protocol is built to stop.

options.label: C
options.text: They fold the accounts into school textbooks as unexplained anomalies beside the ordinary fossil sequence taught in class.
options.rationale: The records are debunked so the baseline stays intact, not added as open anomalies.

options.label: D
options.text: They refile the finds as ordinary geological formations.
options.rationale: The named treatment is the hoax label, not a geological reclassification.

questions.hint: See what is done with historic newspaper accounts and civic records.

questions.question: What leverage remains after the discoverer leaves the site?

options.label: A
options.text: Compulsory psychiatric evaluations by a state medical board, followed by a public note that the finder imagined the garden skull.
options.rationale: Psychiatric boards are not part of the surveillance described.

options.label: B
options.text: Continuous surveillance threats, with the warning that institutional eyes and ears are watching.
options.rationale: Witnesses are told that institutional eyes and ears will be continuously watching and listening.

options.label: C
options.text: Mandatory weekly check-ins at the local police station.
options.rationale: The ongoing pressure is surveillance and the NDA, not a weekly station visit.

options.label: D
options.text: Escrow funds released if the silence continues.
options.rationale: The pressure is threat of ruin, not a payment for staying quiet.

questions.hint: Read what witnesses are told about eyes and ears after the signing.

questions.question: True or False: The storage facilities are sealed away from civilian observation and public air.

options.label: A
options.text: True
options.rationale: The Smithsonian maintains subterranean storage facilities sealed away from civilian observation and public air.

options.label: B
options.text: False
options.rationale: The vaults are sealed away from civilian observation and public air.

questions.hint: Look at how the Smithsonian vaults are described after recovery.

questions.question: True or False: Anomalous finds are allowed to undergo open scientific review.

options.label: A
options.text: True
options.rationale: The system does not allow anomalies to undergo open scientific review.

options.label: B
options.text: False
options.rationale: Rather than allowing anomalies to undergo open scientific review, the system uses a rapid hand-off into institutional custody.

questions.hint: Check what the overview says happens instead of an open review.

questions.question: True or False: The escalation begins when a civilian or builder reports an accidental anatomical find to the local police.

options.label: A
options.text: True
options.rationale: After photographs, the finder notifies the local police department as a non-urgent municipal matter, and that call starts the pipeline.

options.label: B
options.text: False
options.rationale: The sequence does begin with that municipal notification to the local police department.

questions.hint: See what the finder does after photographing the specimen.

questions.question: True or False: Branding discoveries as hoaxes preserves the manufactured historical baseline.

options.label: A
options.text: True
options.rationale: Discoveries branded as hoaxes are dismissed, preserving the manufactured historical baseline without disruption.

options.label: B
options.text: False
options.rationale: The account says that branding the finds as hoaxes preserves the manufactured historical baseline.

questions.hint: Read what the hoax label is said to protect.
